classifications.basis: genuinely concurrent four-request workload matched in both arms; per-attempt aggregate states: attempt 1: 5.239 vs control 62.542 t/s (0.0838x, decisively below the control); attempt 2: 63.794 vs control 62.396 t/s (1.0224x, inside the declared ±5% neutral band). The retained split-arm distribution is highly dispersed (max/min 12.177) while the matched control is stable (max/min 1.002), so the attempt median ratio 0.5525 is recorded per the frozen stop rules but is NOT representative steady-state performance and does not carry the classification. Mechanical basis: no retained attempt demonstrates throughput improvement beyond the neutral band; attempt 1: 5.239 vs control 62.542 t/s (0.0838x, decisively below the control); attempt 2: 63.794 vs control 62.396 t/s (1.0224x, inside the declared ±5% neutral band); the role contributes no separate capacity benefit in this workload. A first-attempt initialization/cold-state effect is observed (large first-versus-second-attempt dispersion); causal attribution is not established by this issue (no retained evidence demonstrates a specific mechanism). Classification: NOT_USEFUL_FOR_TESTED_ROLE.

terminal.basis: utility characterized across the declared roles well enough to distinguish capacity-only versus throughput-useful placements; the measured envelope distinguishes: decisive capacity/residency utility on measured memory-fit facts (x1p-role-capacity ratio 106.5 vs the pressured control); conditional single-sequence throughput utility depending on anchor compute strength (x1p-role-adverse: 1.2601x adding the stronger participant to the weaker anchor vs 0.622x adding the weaker participant to the stronger anchor); unsupported finer split shape on this substrate (x1p-role-adverse-rowsplit-unsupported: fails closed under current supported semantics); no demonstrated benefit for the corrected four-concurrent-request coarse role (median of two highly separated attempts; NOT representative steady-state performance); device/backend compute rate as an explicit crossover input (device-local ratio 2.0259), not an x1/vendor special case.
